$about: THE EXTRACTION ROUND. Branch experiment/base-ui, 11 August 2026.
Three siblings built the SSR naming layer, the i18n layer and the API-shape
closures, all inside one file: packages/ui/src/base-ui-adapter.ts. This round
pulls the ENGINE half of that file into its own workspace package, runs the
full gate chain for the first time since Phase A, and prices what the engine
THE HEADLINE: gate:html is at ZERO. 442 documents graded, 0 violations. The
sequence is 98 (Base UI as composed) → 12 (Phase A) → 0 (now). The SSR
sibling's projection of 0 was a projection with stated evidence; it is now a
THE SECOND HEADLINE, and it is the one that scores the architectural bet:
the extracted package does not import @base-ui/react at all. Not one symbol.
Every fix is a value passed INTO Base UI through a documented prop, and
passing a prop needs no import. React Aria's equivalent defects needed a 27KB
patch of node_modules because the values that had to change were computed
inside the library and never exposed.

$method: `pnpm run verify` was run as one command AND each gate was run
individually, because verify chains with && and halts at gate:registry.
The individual runs are what produced the numbers below; the chained run
confirms it halts where Phase A said it halts and for the same reason.

The GENERATOR runs correctly and emits 107 items; the diff is non-empty because the brief forbids committing. Regenerated diff is +16/-42 lines and is described below.
the_gate_run.gate:smoke: PASS — 107/107 items copied into a bare project and type-checked as a consumer receives them, WITH the new package resolved from node_modules rather than copied. This is the load-bearing evidence that the package/copy-in line was drawn correctly.

the_gate_run.honest_summary: Five of six gates green. The sixth is a git-diff check against a file this brief may not commit, and its generator is green.

dependency_surface.$why_the_peer_range_is_narrow: every fix compensates for an implementation choice, not a documented seam. A patch release can defeat one with no type error and a green build.

what_was_extracted.why_the_strings_left_core: core holds LUMO's invariants. That file is a catalogue of ANOTHER library's English literals, keyed by the dist file and line that emits each one, versioned against Base UI rather than against Lumo. When Base UI ships a translations provider the file is deleted — a lifecycle nothing in core has.

$why: These import types from `react-aria-components`, and a republishable Base
UI package must not have that dependency. The type import is not an
inconvenience — it is the PROOF that these two belong on the other side of
the line. They compensate for LUMO'S FROZEN PUBLIC API (which promises
`onPress` and a React Aria-shaped `onKeyDown`), not for anything Base UI
does wrong. A Base UI-native API deletes them outright; no upstream fix
what_deliberately_STAYED_in_packages_ui.the_distinction_the_extraction_revealed: One file was holding two kinds of code with two different owners, two different lifecycles and two different retirement conditions. That was invisible until something forced the dependency question.

the_distribution_decision.question: package or copy-in companion?
the_distribution_decision.answer: PACKAGE, declared in `dependencies` beside @lumo-ui/core, and removed from SHARED_COMPANIONS
reasoning: Lumo ships by copy-in so a consumer can own and edit what they receive.
That is right for a component. It is WRONG for a workaround against a dated
upstream defect: copied into 107 items it becomes 107 forks of the same
patch, each frozen at the day it was copied, each still shipping after the
bug it works around is fixed. As a package, one `pnpm up` retires it for
every consumer at once — which is the entire point of a workaround having

the_cost.$the_number_a_reader_should_take: 169 lines of code and 446 of comment. The value is not the code — anyone can write 169 lines. It is knowing WHICH 169, and why each obvious alternative (a wrapping <label>, a constant aria-expanded, an unconditional idref, a getAriaValueText on Slider.Root) produces a DIFFERENT defect instead of a fix. Every one of those four was tried and measured wrong by some round of this experiment.

the_package_s_own_suite.tier: renderToStaticMarkup on the `node` environment — jsdom is absent from vitest.config.ts BY CONFIGURATION, with the reason in a docblock
the_package_s_own_suite.$why_that_matters: the suites in packages/ui prove the fixes work through Lumo's components. A package published for strangers has to prove the claim to a stranger: that these are BASE UI defects and that public props close them. Every case renders bare Base UI parts.
poison_twins_that_reproduce_the_defect_f: Field.Root + Field.Label + Checkbox.Root at SSR → control has neither aria-labelledby nor aria-label. ASSERTED, and it passes, so the defect is real at 1.7.0 in this tree.

Field.Description at SSR → the

has an id, the control has no aria-describedby. Base UI mints the id during render; only the REFERENCE is effect-published.
bare Progress.Root value={null} → emits the English literal 'indeterminate progress'.
the_package_s_own_suite.the_most_useful_assertion_in_the_package: the poison twins are asserted to FAIL upstream. If one goes green on a Base UI upgrade, the bug is fixed and the corresponding workaround should be DELETED rather than maintained. That is a deletion trigger built into the test suite.
the_package_s_own_suite.anti_vacuity: the naming case asserts the minted idref RESOLVES to an element and that the element contains the Persian text — not merely that an attribute is present. An attribute pointing at nothing is the second defect class this project tracks.

the_bet_scored_again.question: React Aria's defects needed a 27KB patch of node_modules. Do Base UI's close from outside?
the_bet_scored_again.$the_zero_that_is_the_finding: the third one. The package that exists ENTIRELY to fix Base UI does not import Base UI. Every fix is a value passed in through a documented prop, and passing a prop requires no import. The peer dependency exists to pin the BEHAVIOUR the fixes are verified against, not to link a symbol. A patch must freeze an internal; an adapter only has to understand one.
the_bet_scored_again.internal_paths_READ_for_evidence: several, across rounds — useRegisteredLabelId.js, useAriaLabelledBy.js, ComboboxInternalDismissButton.mjs, SliderThumb.mjs, ProgressRoot.mjs, ToastViewport.mjs. Reading a dist to explain a measured behaviour is not depending on it, and no shipped line imports from any of them.

externally_unfixable_needs_upstream.what: Combobox's internal dismiss sentinel announces 'Dismiss' in every language
externally_unfixable_needs_upstream.why_unfixable: props discarded at the signature; literal after the spread; not importable (83 subpaths, none into combobox/utils/, .d.ts is `export {}`); constructed by parents that forward nothing
externally_unfixable_needs_upstream.upstream: mui/base-ui#5263 — OPEN, maintainer accepted an interim prop in principle

externally_unfixable_needs_upstream.what: Base UI's served <label for> points at its own aria-hidden="true" proxy input, so the association resolves to an element removed from the accessibility tree
externally_unfixable_needs_upstream.why_unfixable: the wrapper can name the control directly (and does), but only upstream can make Base UI's own `for` correct
externally_unfixable_needs_upstream.upstream: part of the unreported SSR-naming report

not_an_accessibility_gap_and_not_externa.what: <Select defaultSelectedKey="thr"> renders the trigger text `thr` where React Aria rendered «تهران». Select.Value resolves a label only from the Root's `items` prop, and the options live in a portal that renders null while closed.
not_an_accessibility_gap_and_not_externa.why_no_adapter_can_fix_it: no ARIA attribute can conjure text that was never rendered. The routes are (a) adopt Base UI's `items` on SelectProps, an additive public API change, or (b) walk children for a matching id and lift its text — a collection builder inside a wrapper, which is the exact work renting a headless library is supposed to buy.
not_an_accessibility_gap_and_not_externa.$the_shape_of_the_remaining_risk: the accessibility layer closes from outside with documented props. The COLLECTION layer does not.

still_open_from_earlier_rounds_and_not_t: number-field-errormessage-is-dropped — RAC's <FieldError> renders the empty string inside a Base UI NumberField.Root, so a caller-supplied validation message never reaches the page in any tier. Root cause is unported form.tsx.
slider description/details wiring — one line, sized in api-shape-gaps.json, never applied.
the 12 inert-prop entries covering 33 prop names argued for REMOVAL in api-shape-gaps.json — none removed; every one is a breaking change.
no `described-controls` gate rule. The aria-describedby half of the naming defect remains ungraded by gate:html.
the date family — Base UI ships no calendar, date-field or time-field primitive. Unchanged and unaddressable by this package.
NO BROWSER rendered anything, in this round or any previous one. Every claim is served bytes, renderToStaticMarkup, or jsdom.

what_it_consists_of: run packages/base-ui-ssr's suite — its poison twins assert bare Base UI is STILL broken; a green twin means delete the workaround
run gate:html over a real build — jsdom cannot see this defect class
diff the eight known English literals against the new dist; a minor that moves one after the spread turns a Persian page English with a green build and no type error
maintenance_per_base_ui_upgrade.compared_to_the_alternative: React Aria's tax was ~11 patch regenerations a year against a permanently closed upstream. This is smaller, cheaper, and — because #5263 got a maintainer reply in five days — has a plausible end date. It is still a tax.

limitations: NOTHING IS COMMITTED. gate:registry cannot pass in this working tree by construction; its generator is green and gate:smoke validates the regenerated manifest.
NO BROWSER. gate:html grades prerendered HTML with linkedom + dom-accessibility-api. No real screen reader has been near any of this.

HYDRATION IS BARELY TESTED. One case in packages/ui checks that a checkbox's hand-wired ids and Base UI's hydrated wiring agree. Select's trigger id is now the wrapper's rather than Base UI's and has no such check. A real hydration-mismatch tier would be needed to claim more.
THE UPSTREAM ISSUE STATES ARE SECOND-HAND. #5263, #5448, #5456, #5457 and #4142 were read via the GitHub API by a sibling agent on 2026-08-11 and are quoted, not re-verified this round.

THE PACKAGE HAS NEVER BEEN PUBLISHED OR INSTALLED FROM A REGISTRY. gate:smoke resolves it through a symlinked node_modules, which is faithful to how a consumer resolves it and is not the same as an npm install.

THE i18n LAYER'S SHIPPED COVERAGE IS STILL 2 OF 7. base-ui-i18n-layer.json's tally is unchanged by this round: three of the seven strings were already closed by required props predating the layer, and two await a Base UI-engine progress.tsx and toast.tsx that do not exist. Extraction moved the code; it closed nothing new.
